text: Lesson 10 showed a broken Avro schema getting rejected, but that has to happen somewhere, checked against something. That's the Schema Registry — a central service storing every version of every topic's schema.
Backward compatible: a new schema can read old data. Forward compatible: an old schema can read new data. Full: both hold at once, the strictest and safest setting.
The producer checks its schema before sending. The Registry validates against the compatibility rule. The consumer looks up the exact schema version embedded in a message to deserialize it correctly.
Confluent Cloud's own Schema Registry, showing the real tree of registered subjects and schema versions for a running cluster.
Both producer and consumer check against the same source of truth, closing the schema-drift problem from Lesson 10. Next up: Kafka Connect.
